body.translated_text: <s>Vaiśeṣikasūtram</s> (The Aphorisms of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> School)
Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty). | KVs_1,1.1 |
That from which results the attainment of <s>abhyudaya</s> (prosperity) and <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (supreme good) is <s>dharma</s>. | KVs_1,1.2 |
The authoritativeness of the <s>Āmnāya</s> (Vedic tradition) is due to its being His word. | KVs_1,1.3 |

body.text: pṛthivy āpas tejo vāyur ākāśaṃ kālo dig ātmā mana iti dravyāṇi | KVs_1,1.4 |
body.translated_text: <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>āpas</s> (water), <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>vāyu</s> (wind), <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>dik</s> (direction), <s>ātman</s> (self), and <s>manas</s> (mind) — these are the <s>dravyas</s> (substances). | KVs_1,1.4 |

body.text: rūparasagandhasparśāḥ saṃkhyāḥ parimāṇāni pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogavibhāgau paratvāparatve buddhayaḥ sukhaduḥkhe icchādveṣau prayatnaś ca guṇāḥ | KVs_1,1.5 |
body.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (color/form), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>gandha</s> (smell), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (remoteness), <s>aparatva</s> (proximity), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), <s>duḥkha</s> (pain), <s>icchā</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>prayatna</s> (effort) — these are the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). | KVs_1,1.5 |

body.text: utkṣepaṇam avakṣepaṇam ākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ gamanam iti karmāṇi | KVs_1,1.6 |
body.translated_text: <s>Utkṣepaṇa</s> (throwing upward), <s>avakṣepaṇa</s> (throwing downward), <s>ākuñcana</s> (contraction), <s>prasāraṇa</s> (expansion), and <s>gamana</s> (motion) — these are the <s>karmans</s> (actions). | KVs_1,1.6 |

body.text: sad anityaṃ dravyavat kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣavad iti dravyaguṇakarmaṇām aviśeṣaḥ | KVs_1,1.7 |
body.translated_text: Being existent, being non-eternal, having <s>dravya</s> (substance) as substratum, being an effect, being a cause, and possessing <s>sāmānya</s> (universals) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particulars) — this is what is common to <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,1.7 |
<s>Dravyas</s> (substances) produce another <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_1,1.8 |
And <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) produce another <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,1.9 |
<s>Karman</s> (action) brought about by another <s>karman</s> (action) does not exist. | KVs_1,1.10 |
<s>Dravya</s> (substance) is not opposed to its effect, nor is it opposed to its cause. | KVs_1,1.11 |
<s>Guṇa</s> (quality) is so in both ways. | KVs_1,1.12 |
<s>Karman</s> (action) is opposed to its effect. | KVs_1,1.13 |

body.text: kriyāvad guṇavat samavāyikāraṇam iti dravyalakṣaṇam | KVs_1,1.14 |
body.translated_text: That which possesses action, possesses qualities, and is an inherent cause — this is the defining mark of <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_1,1.14 |

body.text: dravyāśrayy aguṇavān saṃyogavibhāgeṣv akāraṇam anapekṣa iti guṇalakṣaṇam | KVs_1,1.15 |
body.translated_text: That which resides in a <s>dravya</s> (substance), is itself without qualities, and is not an independent cause in conjunction and disjunction — this is the defining mark of <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,1.15 |

body.text: ekadravyam aguṇaṃ saṃyogavibhāgeṣv anapekṣaṃ kāraṇam iti karmalakṣaṇam | KVs_1,1.16 |
body.translated_text: That which resides in one <s>dravya</s> (substance) only, is without qualities, and is an independent cause of conjunction and disjunction — this is the defining mark of <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,1.16 |
<s>Dravya</s> (substance) is the common cause of <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,1.17 |
So also is <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,1.18 |
<s>Karman</s> (action) is the common cause of conjunction and disjunction. | KVs_1,1.19 |
But not of <s>dravyas</s> (substances), because of their distinction from it. | KVs_1,1.20 |
Nor of <s>karmans</s> (actions), because of the dissimilarity of <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,1.21 |
That the effect of <s>dravyas</s> (substances) is a <s>dravya</s> (substance) is a common property. | KVs_1,1.22 |

body.text: dvitvaprabhṛtayaś ca saṃkhyāḥ pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogavibhāgāś ca | KVs_1,1.23 |
body.translated_text: Duality and the other <s>saṃkhyās</s> (numbers), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), and <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction) also. | KVs_1,1.23 |

body.text: asamavāyāt sāmānyaṃ karma kāryaṃ na vidyate | KVs_1,1.24 |
body.translated_text: Because of non-inherence, <s>karman</s> (action) as a common effect does not exist. | KVs_1,1.24 |
Of conjunctions, <s>dravya</s> (substance) is the common effect. | KVs_1,1.25 |
Of colors, color is the common effect. | KVs_1,1.26 |
Of <s>gurutva</s> (gravity), <s>prayatna</s> (effort), and <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), throwing upward results. | KVs_1,1.27 |
<s>Saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction) result from <s>karmans</s> (actions). | KVs_1,1.28 |
Regarding the common causality of <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>karman</s> (action), it has been stated that <s>karman</s> (action) is not a cause. | KVs_1,1.29 |
From the absence of the cause, the absence of the effect follows. | KVs_1,2.1 |
But not from the absence of the effect the absence of the cause. | KVs_1,2.2 |
<s>Sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) are dependent on cognition. | KVs_1,2.3 |
Existence is only a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal). | KVs_1,2.4 |

body.text: dravyatvaṃ guṇatvaṃ karmatvaṃ ca sāmānyāni viśeṣāś ca | KVs_1,2.5 |
body.translated_text: <s>Dravyatva</s> (substance-ness), <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-ness), and <s>karmatva</s> (action-ness) are both <s>sāmānyas</s> (universals) and <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars). | KVs_1,2.5 |
Except for the ultimate <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars). | KVs_1,2.6 |
"Existent" — because this applies to <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,2.7 |
<s>Sattā</s> (existence/being) is something different from <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,2.8 |
It is not a <s>dravya</s> (substance), because it inheres in only one <s>dravya</s> (substance) at a time. | KVs_1,2.9 |

body.text: guṇakarmasu ca bhāvān na karma na guṇaḥ | KVs_1,2.10 |
body.translated_text: Because it exists in <s>guṇa</s> (quality) and <s>karman</s> (action), it is neither <s>karman</s> (action) nor <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,2.10 |
And because of the absence of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) in it. | KVs_1,2.11 |
<s>Dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) has been explained by its inhering in one <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_1,2.12 |
And by the absence of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular). | KVs_1,2.13 |
<s>Guṇatva</s> (quality-ness) has been explained by its existence in <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_1,2.14 |
And by the absence of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular). | KVs_1,2.15 |
<s>Karmatva</s> (action-ness) has been explained by its existence in <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_1,2.16 |
And by the absence of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular). | KVs_1,2.17 |
Because of the non-difference of the mark of existence, and because of the absence of distinguishing marks, being is one. | KVs_1,2.18 |
<s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color/form), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>gandha</s> (smell), and <s>sparśa</s> (touch). | KVs_2,1.1 |

body.text: rūparasasparśavatya āpo dravāḥ snigdhāś ca | KVs_2,1.2 |
body.translated_text: <s>Āpas</s> (waters) possess <s>rūpa</s> (color/form), <s>rasa</s> (taste), and <s>sparśa</s> (touch); they are fluid and viscous. | KVs_2,1.2 |
<s>Tejas</s> (fire) possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color/form) and <s>sparśa</s> (touch). | KVs_2,1.3 |
<s>Vāyu</s> (wind) possesses <s>sparśa</s> (touch). | KVs_2,1.4 |
These do not exist in <s>ākāśa</s> (space). | KVs_2,1.5 |

body.text: sarpirjatumadhūcchiṣṭānāṃ pārthivānām agnisaṃyogād dravatādbhiḥ sāmānyam | KVs_2,1.6 |
body.translated_text: The fluidity of ghee, lac, beeswax, and other earthly substances upon contact with fire is a commonality with water. | KVs_2,1.6 |

body.text: trapusīsaloharajatasuvarṇānāṃ taijasānām agnisaṃyogād dravatādbhiḥ sāmānyam | KVs_2,1.7 |
body.translated_text: The fluidity of tin, lead, iron, silver, and gold — which are fiery substances — upon contact with fire is a commonality with water. | KVs_2,1.7 |

body.text: viṣāṇī kakudmān prāntevāladhiḥ sāsnāvān iti gotve dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgam | KVs_2,1.8 |
body.translated_text: Having horns, having a hump, having a tail with hair at the end, and having a dewlap — these are the observed marks of <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness). | KVs_2,1.8 |
And <s>sparśa</s> (touch) also. | KVs_2,1.9 |

body.text: na ca dṛṣṭānāṃ sparśa ity adṛṣṭaliṅgo vāyuḥ | KVs_2,1.10 |
body.translated_text: Since the touch of visible things is not such, <s>vāyu</s> (wind) is known by an unperceived mark. | KVs_2,1.10 |
Because it does not inhere in another <s>dravya</s> (substance), it is a <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_2,1.11 |
Because it possesses action and because it possesses qualities. | KVs_2,1.12 |

body.text: adravyavattvena nityatvam uktam (C,BhV) (V adravyatvenānityam, U adravyatvena) | KVs_2,1.13 |
body.translated_text: Its eternality has been explained by its not inhering in another <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_2,1.13 |
The mutual collision of <s>vāyu</s> (wind) with <s>vāyu</s> (wind) is the mark of its plurality. | KVs_2,1.14 |

body.text: vāyor iti sati snnikarṣe pratyakṣābhāvād dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ na vidyate | KVs_2,1.15 |
body.translated_text: Even when there is contact with <s>vāyu</s> (wind), because there is no direct perception, no observed mark exists. | KVs_2,1.15 |
And there is no distinction from what is perceived through general inference. | KVs_2,1.16 |
Therefore, it is known through <s>āgama</s> (scriptural testimony). | KVs_2,1.17 |
But the act of naming is the mark of beings distinguished from us. | KVs_2,1.18 |
Because the act of naming is preceded by direct perception. | KVs_2,1.19 |

body.text: niṣkramaṇaṃ praveśanam ity ākāśasya liṅgam | KVs_2,1.20 |
body.translated_text: Going out and entering in — these are the marks of <s>ākāśa</s> (space). | KVs_2,1.20 |
That is not a valid mark, because <s>karman</s> (action) inheres in only one <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_2,1.21 |
And because of dissimilarity from the operation of other causes. | KVs_2,1.22 |
From conjunction, the absence of <s>karman</s> (action) results. | KVs_2,1.23 |

body.text: kāraṇaguṇapūrvaḥ kārye guṇo dṛṣṭaḥ kāryāntarāprādurbhāvāc ca śabdaḥ sparśavatām aguṇaḥ | KVs_2,1.24 |
body.translated_text: A <s>guṇa</s> (quality) in the effect is observed to be preceded by the <s>guṇa</s> (quality) of the cause; and since no other effect is produced, <s>śabda</s> (sound) is not a quality of things possessing <s>sparśa</s> (touch). | KVs_2,1.24 |

body.text: paratra samavāyāt pratyakṣatvāc ca nātmaguṇo na manoguṇaḥ | KVs_2,1.25 |
body.translated_text: Because it inheres elsewhere and because of its perceptibility, it is neither a quality of the <s>ātman</s> (self) nor a quality of <s>manas</s> (mind). | KVs_2,1.25 |
This is the mark of <s>ākāśa</s> (space). | KVs_2,1.26 |
Its <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and <s>nityatva</s> (eternality) have been explained by the analogy of <s>vāyu</s> (wind). | KVs_2,1.27 |

children.text: puṣpavastrayoḥ sati sannikarṣe gandhāntarāprādurbhāvo vastre gandhābhāvaliṅgam | KVs_2,2.1 |
children.translated_text: When a flower and a cloth are in contact, the non-appearance of a different smell in the cloth is the mark of the absence of smell in the cloth. | KVs_2,2.1 |
By this, the heat in water has been explained. | KVs_2,2.2 |
<s>Gandha</s> (smell) is established in <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth). | KVs_2,2.3 |
Heat is in <s>tejas</s> (fire). | KVs_2,2.4 |
Coldness is in <s>āpas</s> (water). | KVs_2,2.5 |

children.text: aparasmin paraṃ yugapad ayugapac ciraṃ kṣipram iti kālaliṅgāni | KVs_2,2.6 |
children.translated_text: "Later in relation to the other," "earlier," "simultaneously," "not simultaneously," "slowly," "quickly" — these are the marks of <s>kāla</s> (time). | KVs_2,2.6 |
Its <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and <s>nityatva</s> (eternality) have been explained by the analogy of <s>vāyu</s> (wind). | KVs_2,2.7 |
Its reality is established by its existence. | KVs_2,2.8 |
Its plurality is established by the diversity of effects. | KVs_2,2.9 |
Because of its absence in eternal things and its presence in non-eternal things. | KVs_2,2.10 |
In the ultimate cause, it is designated as <s>kāla</s> (time). | KVs_2,2.11 |

children.text: ita idam iti yatas tad diśo liṅgam | KVs_2,2.12 |
children.translated_text: "From here," "from there" — that from which such usage arises is the mark of <s>dik</s> (direction). | KVs_2,2.12 |
Its <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and <s>nityatva</s> (eternality) have been explained by the analogy of <s>vāyu</s> (wind). | KVs_2,2.13 |
Its reality is established by its existence. | KVs_2,2.14 |
Its plurality is established by the diversity of effects. | KVs_2,2.15 |

children.text: ādityasaṃyogād bhūtapūrvād bhaviṣyato bhūtāc ca prācī | KVs_2,2.16 |
children.translated_text: From conjunction with the sun — past, future, and present — the east is established. | KVs_2,2.16 |

children.text: tathā dakṣiṇā pratīcy udīci ca | KVs_2,2.17 |
children.translated_text: Similarly, the south, west, and north. | KVs_2,2.17 |
By this, the intermediate directions have been explained. | KVs_2,2.18 |

children.text: sāmānyapratyakṣād viśeṣāpratyakṣād viśeṣasmṛteś ca saṃśayaḥ | KVs_2,2.19 |
children.translated_text: Doubt arises from the perception of a common property, the non-perception of a distinguishing property, and the recollection of a distinguishing property. | KVs_2,2.19 |
It concerns both the seen and the unseen. | KVs_2,2.20 |
And the seen is like what has been seen before. | KVs_2,2.21 |
The seen may be as seen, as not seen, or as both, because of being perceived in both ways. | KVs_2,2.22 |
And doubt arises from knowledge and ignorance. | KVs_2,2.23 |
That object which is apprehended by the ear is <s>śabda</s> (sound). | KVs_2,2.24 |

children.text: tasmin dravyaṃ karma guṇa iti saṃśayaḥ | KVs_2,2.25 |
children.translated_text: Regarding it, there is doubt whether it is a <s>dravya</s> (substance), a <s>karman</s> (action), or a <s>guṇa</s> (quality). | KVs_2,2.25 |

children.text: tulyajātīyeṣv arthāntarabhūteṣu ca viśeṣasyobhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt | KVs_2,2.26 |
children.translated_text: Because among things of the same class and things of different classes, the distinguishing mark is observed in both ways. | KVs_2,2.26 |
It is not a <s>dravya</s> (substance), because it inheres in only one <s>dravya</s> (substance). | KVs_2,2.27 |
It is not a <s>karman</s> (action), because it is not visible. | KVs_2,2.28 |
The cessation of an existing <s>guṇa</s> (quality) is its similarity with <s>karman</s> (action). | KVs_2,2.29 |
Because of the absence of a mark of the existent. | KVs_2,2.30 |
Because of dissimilarity with the eternal. | KVs_2,2.31 |
Because it is a product. | KVs_2,2.32 |
Because of its non-existence before production. | KVs_2,2.33 |
Because of modification from a cause. | KVs_2,2.34 |
Because of defects. | KVs_2,2.35 |

children.text: saṃyogād vibhāgāc chabdāc ca śabdaniṣpatteḥ | KVs_2,2.36 |
children.translated_text: From conjunction, from disjunction, and from <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>śabda</s> (sound) is produced. | KVs_2,2.36 |
And from the marks, it is non-eternal. | KVs_2,2.37 |
But because of the absence of both kinds of activity. | KVs_2,2.38 |
Because of the absence of number. | KVs_2,2.39 |
Because of the original sound. | KVs_2,2.40 |
And because of agreed usage. | KVs_2,2.41 |
They are uncertain when there are many. | KVs_2,2.42 |
The absence of number is in general. | KVs_2,2.43 |

body.translated_text: Its reality is established by its existence. | KVs_2,1.28 |
The objects of the senses are well-established. | KVs_3,1.1 |
The well-established nature of sense-objects is the ground for their being different from the senses. | KVs_3,1.2 |
That is without designation. | KVs_3,1.3 |
Because of ignorance of the cause. | KVs_3,1.4 |
Because of ignorance of the effect. | KVs_3,1.5 |
And [a fallacious reason arises] from ignorance. [KVs 3.1.6]

body.text: anya eva hetur ity anapadeśaḥ | KVs_3,1.7 |
body.translated_text: That [the reason] is entirely different — this is a non-reason (<s>anapadeśa</s>). [KVs 3.1.7]

body.text: saṃyogi samavāyy ekārthasamavāyi virodhi ca, kāryaṃ kāryāntarasya, kāraṇaṃ kāraṇāntarasya, virodhy abhūtaṃ bhūtasya, bhūtam abhūtasya, abhūtam abhūtasya, bhūtaṃ bhūtasya | KVs_3,1.8 |
body.translated_text: That which is conjoined (<s>saṃyogin</s>), inherent (<s>samavāyin</s>), co-inherent in the same substrate (<s>ekārthasamavāyin</s>), and contradictory (<s>virodhin</s>) — an effect [can serve as a reason] for another effect, a cause for another cause, a contradictory [reason] for what is non-existent with respect to what exists, what exists with respect to what is non-existent, what is non-existent with respect to what is non-existent, and what exists with respect to what exists. [KVs 3.1.8]
Because a valid reason (<s>apadeśa</s>) must be preceded by what is well-established (<s>prasiddha</s>). [KVs 3.1.9]
What is not well-established is a non-reason (<s>anapadeśa</s>). [KVs 3.1.10]
What is non-existent and what is doubtful are also non-reasons. [KVs 3.1.11]

body.text: viṣāṇī tasmād aśvo viṣāṇī tasmād gaur iti ca | KVs_3,1.12 |
body.translated_text: 'It has horns, therefore it is a horse; it has horns, therefore it is a cow' — [these illustrate fallacious reasoning]. [KVs 3.1.12]

body.text: ātmendriyamano'rthasannikarṣād yan niṣpadyate tad anyat | KVs_3,1.13 |
body.translated_text: What is produced from the contact of <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>indriya</s> (sense organ), <s>manas</s> (mind), and <s>artha</s> (object) — that is different [from inference]. [KVs 3.1.13]

body.text: pravṛttinivṛttī ca pratyagātmani dṛṣṭe paratra liṅgam | KVs_3,1.14 |
body.translated_text: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), observed in one's own self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), are the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) [of the self] in others. [KVs 3.1.14]

body.text: ātmendriyārthasannikarṣe jñānasyābhāvo bhāvaś ca manaso liṅgam | KVs_3,2.1 |
body.translated_text: When there is contact of <s>ātman</s>, <s>indriya</s>, and <s>artha</s>, the absence and presence of cognition is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>manas</s> (mind). [KVs 3.2.1]
Its substantiality (<s>dravyatva</s>) and eternality (<s>nityatva</s>) have been explained by [the analogy with] <s>vāyu</s> (air). [KVs 3.2.2]
From the non-simultaneity of volitions (<s>prayatna</s>) and the non-simultaneity of cognitions, <s>manas</s> is one [i.e., atomic]. [KVs 3.2.3]

body.text: prāṇāpānanimeṣonmeṣajīvanamanogatīndriyāntaravikārāḥ sukhaduḥkhe icchādveṣau prayatnaś cety ātmaliṅgāni | KVs_3,2.4 |
body.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> (in-breath), <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), closing of the eyes, opening of the eyes, life, mental movement, sensory transformations, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and volition (<s>prayatna</s>) — these are the marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>ātman</s>. [KVs 3.2.4]
Its substantiality and eternality have been explained by [the analogy with] <s>vāyu</s>. [KVs 3.2.5]

body.text: yajñadatta iti sati sannikarṣe pratyakṣābhāvād dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ na vidyate | KVs_3,2.6 |
body.translated_text: In the case of <s>Yajñadatta</s>, when there is contact [of senses with the self], there is no perception — therefore no observable inferential mark exists [for the self]. [KVs 3.2.6]
And from inference based on general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>), there is no specific determination [of the individual self]. [KVs 3.2.7]
Therefore [knowledge of the self] is based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>). [KVs 3.2.8]
Because the word 'I' is distinct [from scriptural testimony], [the knowledge of self] is not [merely] scriptural. [KVs 3.2.9]

body.text: yadi ca dṛṣṭapratyakṣo 'haṃ devadatto 'haṃ yajñadatta iti | KVs_3,2.10 |
body.translated_text: If [it is argued that] the self is perceived through direct perception — 'I am <s>Devadatta</s>,' 'I am <s>Yajñadatta</s>.' [KVs 3.2.10]

body.text: devadatto gacchati viṣṇumitro gacchatīti copacārāc charīrapratyakṣaḥ | KVs_3,2.11 |
body.translated_text: '<s>Devadatta</s> goes,' '<s>Viṣṇumitra</s> goes' — by such conventional usage (<s>upacāra</s>), it is the body that is [actually] perceived. [KVs 3.2.11]
But the conventional usage is doubtful. [KVs 3.2.12]

body.text: aham iti pratyagātmani bhāvāt paratrābhāvād arthāntarapratyakṣaḥ | KVs_3,2.13 |
body.translated_text: Because the [cognition] 'I' exists in one's own self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) and is absent in others, [the self] is perceived as something different [from the body]. [KVs 3.2.13]

body.text: na tu śarīraviśeṣād yajñadattaviṣṇumitrayor jñānaviśeṣaḥ | KVs_3,2.14 |
body.translated_text: The difference in cognition between <s>Yajñadatta</s> and <s>Viṣṇumitra</s> is not due to difference in body. [KVs 3.2.14]
From the non-difference in the production of pleasure, pain, and cognition, [one might conclude] the unity of all selves (<s>aikātmya</s>). [KVs 3.2.15]
[But selves are] many, because of distinct [karmic] arrangements (<s>vyavasthā</s>). [KVs 3.2.16]
And because of the authority of scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). [KVs 3.2.17]
That which exists and has no cause — that is eternal (<s>nitya</s>). [KVs 4.1.1]
Its effect is the inferential mark [of the non-eternal]. [KVs 4.1.2]
For the existence of the effect [follows] from the existence of the cause. [KVs 4.1.3]
'Non-eternal' — this is the negation of the [eternal] particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>). [KVs 4.1.4]
And [it arises from] ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). [KVs 4.1.5]
In a large [substance], perception [of color] arises because it possesses many substances and because of [visible] color (<s>rūpa</s>). [KVs 4.1.6]
In the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), there is no perception, because it does not possess [multiple] substances. [KVs 4.1.7]
In <s>vāyu</s> (air), there is no perception [of color], because of the absence of color and [color-]impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). [KVs 4.1.8]

body.text: anekadravyeṇa dravyeṇa samavāyād rūpaviśeṣāc copalabdhiḥ | KVs_4,1.9 |
body.translated_text: Perception [arises] from inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) in a substance possessing many substances, and from a specific color. [KVs 4.1.9]
By this, cognition of taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>) has been explained. [KVs 4.1.10]
From the absence of that [color etc. in certain substances], there is no deviation [from the rule]. [KVs 4.1.11]

body.text: saṃkhyāḥ parimāṇāni pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogavibhāgau paratvāparatve karma ca rūpidravyasamavāyāc cākṣuṣāṇi | KVs_4,1.12 |
body.translated_text: Number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), remoteness (<s>paratva</s>), proximity (<s>aparatva</s>), and action (<s>karma</s>) — these are visible [i.e., perceptible by the eye] through inherence in a substance possessing color. [KVs 4.1.12]
In colorless [substances], they are not visible. [KVs 4.1.13]

body.text: etena guṇatve bhāve ca sarvendriyajñānaṃ vyākhyātam | KVs_4,1.14 |
body.translated_text: By this, cognition through all sense organs of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and existence (<s>bhāva</s>) has been explained. [KVs 4.1.14]

body.text: pratyakṣāpratyakṣāṇām apratyakṣatvāt saṃyogasya pañcātmakaṃ na vidyate | KVs_4,2.1 |
body.translated_text: Because conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) of perceptible and imperceptible [substances] is imperceptible, a five-element compound does not exist. [KVs 4.2.1]

body.text: guṇāntarāprādurbhāvāc ca tryātmakam api na | KVs_4,2.2 |
body.translated_text: And because no new qualities emerge, not even a three-element [compound exists]. [KVs 4.2.2]

body.text: ātmasaṃyogas tv avipratiṣiddho mithaḥ pañcānām | KVs_4,2.3 |
body.translated_text: But the mutual conjunction of the five [elements] with the <s>ātman</s> is not contradicted. [KVs 4.2.3]
Because [conjunction] is preceded by [the elements existing in] multiple locations. [KVs 4.2.4]
Because of a specific <s>dharma</s> (unseen merit). [KVs 4.2.5]
Because of a specific effect. [KVs 4.2.6]
Because there is no [established] name [for such a compound]. [KVs 4.2.7]
Because [beings] possess names and the like. [KVs 4.2.8]
There exist beings not born from a womb (<s>ayonija</s>), and [this is known] from the mark of the <s>Veda</s>. [KVs 4.2.9]
Action in the hand [arises] from the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and volition (<s>prayatna</s>). [KVs 5.1.1]
Similarly, the action of the pestle (<s>musala</s>) [arises] from conjunction with the hand. [KVs 5.1.2]

body.text: abhighātaje musalakarmaṇi vyatirekād akāraṇaṃ hastasaṃyogaḥ | KVs_5,1.3 |
body.translated_text: In the action of the pestle produced by a blow (<s>abhighāta</s>), the conjunction with the hand is not the cause, by [the principle of] exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>). [KVs 5.1.3]
Similarly, the conjunction with the <s>ātman</s> [is not the cause] of the action of the hand and pestle [produced by a blow]. [KVs 5.1.4]

body.text: musalābhighātāt tu musalasaṃyogād dhaste karma | KVs_5,1.5 |
body.translated_text: But from the blow of the pestle and the conjunction with the pestle, [there arises] action in the hand. [KVs 5.1.5]
Similarly, the action of the <s>ātman</s> [arises] from conjunction with the hand as well. [KVs 5.1.6]
In the absence of conjunction [with a support], falling [occurs] due to gravity (<s>gurutva</s>). [KVs 5.1.7]

body.text: nodanaviśeṣābhāvād nordhvaṃ na tiryag gamanam | KVs_5,1.8 |
body.translated_text: In the absence of a specific impulsion (<s>nodana</s>), there is neither upward nor lateral movement. [KVs 5.1.8]
From a specific volition (<s>prayatna</s>) arises a specific impulsion. [KVs 5.1.9]
From a specific impulsion arises a specific throwing upward. [KVs 5.1.10]
By [the explanation of] the action of the hand, the action of a child [or ball] has been explained. [KVs 5.1.11]
Similarly, the bursting open of something burnt [is explained]. [KVs 5.1.12]
In the absence of volition, a sleeping person falls due to gravity. [KVs 5.1.13]
The movement of grass [is caused] by conjunction with <s>vāyu</s> (wind). [KVs 5.1.14]
The movement of a magnet [toward iron] and the movement of a needle [toward a magnet] — these are caused by the unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). [KVs 5.1.15]

body.text: iṣāv ayugapat saṃyogaviśeṣāḥ karmānyatve hetuḥ | KVs_5,1.16 |
body.translated_text: In an arrow, the non-simultaneous specific conjunctions are the reason [for inferring] that each successive action is different. [KVs 5.1.16]

body.text: nodanād ādyam iṣoḥ karma karmakāritāc ca saṃskārād uttaraṃ tathottaram uttaraṃ ca | KVs_5,1.17 |
body.translated_text: The first action of the arrow [arises] from impulsion (<s>nodana</s>); from the impressed force (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced by that action [arises] the subsequent [action], and similarly each successive one. [KVs 5.1.17]
In the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> (impressed force), falling [occurs] due to gravity. [KVs 5.1.18]

body.text: nodanād abhighātāt saṃyuktasaṃyogāc ca pṛthivyāṃ karma | KVs_5,2.1 |
body.translated_text: In earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), action [arises] from impulsion, from impact (<s>abhighāta</s>), and from conjunction with what is [itself] conjoined. [KVs 5.2.1]
That [action of earth is], in particular cases, caused by the unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). [KVs 5.2.2]
In the absence of conjunction [with a support], water (<s>ap</s>) falls due to gravity. [KVs 5.2.3]
That [falling of water is], in particular cases, caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. [KVs 5.2.4]
Flowing (<s>syandana</s>) [of water occurs] due to fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>). [KVs 5.2.5]
Rising [of water] through a tube (<s>nāḍī</s>) [occurs] due to conjunction with <s>vāyu</s>. [KVs 5.2.6]
[Action of water also arises] from impulsion, from pressure (<s>pīḍana</s>), and from conjunction with what is conjoined. [KVs 5.2.7]
The creeping [of water] toward trees — this is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. [KVs 5.2.8]

body.text: apāṃ saṅghāto vilayanaṃ ca tejasaḥ saṃyogāt | KVs_5,2.9 |
body.translated_text: The solidification of water and the melting [of solids occur] from conjunction with <s>tejas</s> (fire). [KVs 5.2.9]
In that [process], lightning (<s>avasphūrjathu</s>) is the inferential mark. [KVs 5.2.10]
And [this is confirmed by] Vedic [testimony]. [KVs 5.2.11]

body.text: apāṃ saṃyogād vibhāgāc ca stanayitnuḥ | KVs_5,2.12 |
body.translated_text: From the conjunction and disjunction of water [particles], thunder (<s>stanayitnu</s>) [arises]. [KVs 5.2.12]

body.text: pṛthivīkarmaṇā tejaḥkarma vāyukarma ca vyākhyātam | KVs_5,2.13 |
body.translated_text: By [the explanation of] the action of earth, the action of fire (<s>tejas</s>) and the action of wind (<s>vāyu</s>) have been explained. [KVs 5.2.13]

body.text: agner ūrdhvajvalanaṃ vāyoś ca tiryagpavanam aṇumanasoś cādyaṃ karmety adṛṣṭakāritāni | KVs_5,2.14 |
body.translated_text: The upward flaming of fire, the lateral blowing of wind, and the initial action of atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) and <s>manas</s> — these are caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. [KVs 5.2.14]
By [the explanation of] the action of the hand, the action of <s>manas</s> has been explained. [KVs 5.2.15]
From the contact of <s>ātman</s>, <s>indriya</s>, <s>manas</s>, and <s>artha</s>, pleasure and pain [arise]; the cessation of that [contact is the cessation of pleasure and pain]. [KVs 5.2.16]

body.text: ātmasthe manasi saśarīrasya sukhaduḥkhābhāvaḥ sa yogaḥ | KVs_5,2.17 |
body.translated_text: When <s>manas</s> rests in the <s>ātman</s> [alone], there is absence of pleasure and pain for the embodied being — that is <s>yoga</s>. [KVs 5.2.17]
By [the explanation of] bodily action, the action of the <s>ātman</s> has been explained. [KVs 5.2.18]

body.text: apasarpaṇam upasarpaṇam aśitapītasaṃyogaḥ kāryāntarasaṃyogāś cety adṛṣṭakāritāni | KVs_5,2.19 |
body.translated_text: Moving away, moving toward, the conjunction of what is eaten and drunk, and conjunctions with other effects — these are caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. [KVs 5.2.19]
In the absence of that [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>], the absence of conjunction and non-manifestation [of the body] — that is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). [KVs 5.2.20]
Darkness (<s>tamas</s>) is merely the absence of being (<s>bhāva</s>), due to its dissimilarity with substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and action (<s>karma</s>). [KVs 5.2.21]
And [darkness arises] from the obstruction of <s>tejas</s> (light) by another substance. [KVs 5.2.22]

body.text: dikkālāv ākāśaṃ ca kriyāvadbhyo vaidharmyān niṣkriyāṇi | KVs_5,2.23 |
body.translated_text: Direction (<s>dik</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>) are without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>), due to their dissimilarity from things that possess action. [KVs 5.2.23]

body.text: etena karmāṇi guṇāś ca vyākhyātāḥ | KVs_5,2.24 |
body.translated_text: By this, actions (<s>karma</s>) and qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) [of direction, time, and space] have been explained. [KVs 5.2.24]
Inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) with actions is denied for those that are without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>). [KVs 5.2.25]
But the qualities that are non-inherent [in them] are [their] cause. [KVs 5.2.26]
By [the explanation of] qualities, direction (<s>dik</s>) has been explained. [KVs 5.2.27]
By [the explanation of] cause, time (<s>kāla</s>) [has been explained]. [KVs 5.2.28]
The composition of sentences in the <s>Veda</s> is preceded by intelligence (<s>buddhi</s>). [KVs 6.1.1]
But [the authoritativeness of the <s>Veda</s>] is not to be inferred from our [ordinary human] cognitions as the mark of a <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer). [KVs 6.1.2]
Similarly, in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts], the establishment of conventional names and rituals is the [inferential] mark [of intelligent authorship]. [KVs 6.1.3]
The act of giving (<s>dadāti</s>) is preceded by intelligence. [KVs 6.1.4]
Similarly, the act of receiving (<s>pratigraha</s>). [KVs 6.1.5]
The sequence of those two [giving and receiving] is like that of [acts] which are not subsidiary to each other. [KVs 6.1.6]
Because the qualities of one self are not the cause of the qualities of another self. [KVs 6.1.7]
From eating what is not defiled (<s>aduṣṭa</s>), and from [appropriate] ritualistic recitation (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>), [arises] prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>). [KVs 6.1.8]
That [prosperity] does not exist in [the case of eating] defiled food. [KVs 6.1.9]
What is defiled [is so] because of [its connection with] injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>). [KVs 6.1.10]
From [inappropriate] ritualistic recitation, [there arises] fault (<s>doṣa</s>). [KVs 6.1.11]
That [fault] does not exist in what is not defiled. [KVs 6.1.12]
One should give to the superior [recipient]. [KVs 6.1.13]
One should not give to the equal or the inferior. [KVs 6.1.14]
By this, the [rules for] receiving from inferior, equal, and superior persons of <s>dharma</s> have been explained. [KVs 6.1.15]
Similarly, the renunciation of conflicting [activities is prescribed]. [KVs 6.1.16]
When [the recipient is] equal, [it is a matter of choice between] giving up one's own [possession] or giving up another's. [KVs 6.1.17]
When [the recipient is] superior, one should give up one's own [possession]. [KVs 6.1.18]

body.text: dṛṣṭānāṃ dṛṣṭaprayojanānāṃ dṛṣṭābhāve prayogo 'bhyudayāya.(C,V) (U dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaprayojanānāṃ dṛṣṭābhāve prayojanam abhyudayāya.) | KVs_6,2.1 |
body.translated_text: Of actions having both visible and invisible purposes, in the absence of a visible [purpose], the application is for <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity). (Variant: Of actions having visible and invisible purposes, in the absence of a visible [purpose], the purpose is for <s>abhyudaya</s>.) | KVs 6.2.1 |

Ritual bathing (<s>abhiṣecana</s>), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), dwelling in the teacher's house (<s>gurukulavāsa</s>), the forest-hermit life (<s>vānaprasthya</s>), sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>), observance of directions, asterisms, mantras, and time-rules — [these are] for the invisible [purpose] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). | KVs 6.2.2 |

children.translated_text: The fault of [mere] existence is qualified [fault] (<s>upadhā</s>). | KVs 6.2.4 |
The absence of fault is unqualified (<s>anupadhā</s>). | KVs 6.2.5 |

children.text: iṣṭarūparasagandhasparśaṃ prokṣitam abhyukṣitaṃ ca tac chuci | KVs_6,2.6 |
children.translated_text: That which, having the desired color, taste, smell, and touch, is sprinkled and ritually bathed — that is pure (<s>śuci</s>). | KVs 6.2.6 |
'Impure' (<s>aśuci</s>) is the negation of 'pure.' | KVs 6.2.7 |
And [it is] a distinct category. | KVs 6.2.8 |

children.text: ayatasya śucibhojanād abhyudayo na vidyate yamābhāvāt | KVs_6,2.9 |
children.translated_text: For one who is undisciplined, there is no <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity) from eating pure food, due to the absence of discipline (<s>yama</s>). | KVs 6.2.9 |
And there is [prosperity], because discipline (<s>yama</s>) is a distinct category. | KVs 6.2.10 |
And in its absence, [there is no prosperity] because of non-existence. | KVs 6.2.11 |
From pleasure [arises] attachment (<s>rāga</s>). | KVs 6.2.12 |
And because of being absorbed in that [pleasure]. | KVs 6.2.13 |
And from satisfaction (<s>tṛpti</s>). | KVs 6.2.14 |
And from <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (the unseen). | KVs 6.2.15 |
And from a particular birth (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>), a particular attachment (<s>rāgaviśeṣa</s>) [arises]. | KVs 6.2.16 |
Activity toward <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is preceded by desire (<s>icchā</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). | KVs 6.2.17 |
From that [arise] conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>). | KVs 6.2.18 |
<s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) has been explained [in the discussion] of the actions of the self (<s>ātmakarma</s>). | KVs 6.2.19 |

body.translated_text: The four stages of life (<s>cāturāśramya</s>), [observances] with qualification (<s>upadhā</s>) and without qualification (<s>anupadhā</s>). | KVs 6.2.3 |
Qualities have been stated. | KVs 7.1.1 |
And the definition of quality has been stated. | KVs 7.1.2 |

body.text: idam evaṃguṇam idam evaṃguṇam iti coktam | KVs_7,1.3 |
body.translated_text: 'This has such qualities, this has such qualities' — thus too has been stated. | KVs 7.1.3 |
In earth, color, taste, smell, and touch are non-eternal, because the substance is non-eternal. | KVs 7.1.4 |
And because of conjunction with fire. | KVs 7.1.5 |
Because of the manifestation of different qualities. | KVs 7.1.6 |
By this, the non-eternality [of qualities] in eternal [substances] is stated. | KVs 7.1.7 |

body.text: apsu tejasi vāyau ca nityā dravyanityatvāt | KVs_7,1.8 |
body.translated_text: In water, fire, and air, [qualities are] eternal, because the substance is eternal. | KVs 7.1.8 |
In non-eternal [substances], [qualities are] non-eternal, because the substance is non-eternal. | KVs 7.1.9 |
In earth, those [qualities] produced by heat (<s>pākaja</s>) are preceded by the qualities of the cause. | KVs 7.1.10 |

body.text: apsu tejasi vāyau ca kāraṇaguṇapūrvāḥ pākajā na vidyante | KVs_7,1.11 |
body.translated_text: In water, fire, and air, [qualities are] preceded by the qualities of the cause; those produced by heat (<s>pākaja</s>) do not exist [in them]. | KVs 7.1.11 |

body.text: aguṇavato dravyasya guṇārambhāt karmaguṇā aguṇāḥ | KVs_7,1.12 |
body.translated_text: Because of the origination of qualities in a substance devoid of qualities, the qualities of actions and qualities are without [further] qualities. | KVs 7.1.12 |
By this, those produced by heat (<s>pākaja</s>) are explained. | KVs 7.1.13 |
Because of being [inhering] in one substance. | KVs 7.1.14 |

body.text: aṇor mahataś copalabdhyanupalabdhī nitye vyākhyāte | KVs_7,1.15 |
body.translated_text: The perception and non-perception of the atomic and the great in eternal [substances] has been explained. | KVs 7.1.15 |

body.text: kāraṇabahutvāt kāraṇamahattvāt pracayaviśeṣāc ca mahat | KVs_7,1.16 |
body.translated_text: Because of the multiplicity of causes, because of the greatness of the cause, and because of a particular accumulation, [something is] great. | KVs 7.1.16 |
The opposite of that is the atom (<s>aṇu</s>). | KVs 7.1.17 |

body.text: aṇu mahad iti tasmin viśeṣabhāvād viśeṣābhāvāc ca | KVs_7,1.18 |
body.translated_text: 'Atomic' and 'great' — because of the presence of a specific [quality] in that, and because of the absence of a specific [quality]. | KVs 7.1.18 |
Because of simultaneity. | KVs 7.1.19 |
The absence of atomic-ness and great-ness in atomic-ness and great-ness has been explained through actions and qualities. | KVs 7.1.21 |
The actions and qualities [explained] by atomic-ness and great-ness are without [further] qualities. | KVs 7.1.22 |
By this, length (<s>dīrghatva</s>) and shortness (<s>hrasvatva</s>) are explained. | KVs 7.1.23 |
Actions [are explained] by actions, and qualities by qualities. | KVs 7.1.24 |
That [dimension is non-eternal] in a non-eternal [substance]. | KVs 7.1.25 |
The spherical (<s>parimaṇḍala</s>) [dimension of the atom] is eternal. | KVs 7.1.26 |
And ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the mark of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). | KVs 7.1.27 |
Because of all-pervasiveness, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is great. | KVs 7.1.28 |
And likewise the self (<s>ātman</s>). | KVs 7.1.29 |
Because of the absence of that [all-pervasiveness], the mind (<s>manas</s>) is atomic. | KVs 7.1.30 |
Direction (<s>dik</s>) is explained through qualities. | KVs 7.1.31 |
Time (<s>kāla</s>) [is explained] through the cause. | KVs 7.1.32 |

body.text: rūparasagandhasparśavyatirekād arthāntaram ekatvaṃ tathā pṛthaktvam | KVs_7,2.1 |
body.translated_text: Distinct from color, taste, smell, and touch — oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) is a separate category; likewise, separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>). | KVs 7.2.1 |

body.text: tayor nityatvānityatve tejaso rūpasparśābhyāṃ vyākhyāte | KVs_7,2.2 |
body.translated_text: The eternality and non-eternality of those two [oneness and separateness] have been explained by [analogy with] the color and touch of fire. | KVs 7.2.2 |
And [their] production. | KVs 7.2.3 |
The absence of single-oneness and single-separateness in oneness and separateness. | KVs 7.2.4 |
Actions by actions, qualities by qualities. | KVs 7.2.5 |

body.text: niḥsaṃkhyatvāt karmaguṇānāṃ sarvaikatvaṃ na vidyate | KVs_7,2.6 |
body.translated_text: Because of the innumerability of actions and qualities, universal oneness does not exist. | KVs 7.2.6 |
Because of the absence of oneness, division [into parts] does not exist. | KVs 7.2.7 |
Because of the absence of single-oneness and single-separateness in the cause and effect [pair], oneness and separateness [of cause and effect] do not exist. | KVs 7.2.8 |
This has been explained for non-eternal [entities]. | KVs 7.2.9 |

body.text: anyatarakarmaja ubhayakarmajaḥ saṃyogajaś ca saṃyogaḥ | KVs_7,2.10 |
body.translated_text: Conjunction [arises] from the action of one, from the action of both, and from [prior] conjunction. | KVs 7.2.10 |
By this, disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>) is explained. | KVs 7.2.11 |
The absence of conjunction and disjunction in conjunction and disjunction has been explained by [analogy with] atomic-ness and great-ness. | KVs 7.2.12 |
Actions by actions, qualities by qualities. | KVs 7.2.13 |

body.text: yutasiddhyabhāvāt kāryakāraṇayoḥ saṃyogavibhāgau na vidyete | KVs_7,2.14 |
body.translated_text: Because of the absence of separate existence (<s>yutasiddhi</s>), conjunction and disjunction do not exist in the cause-and-effect [relation]. | KVs 7.2.14 |
Because of being a quality. | KVs 7.2.15 |
A quality too is conceived. | KVs 7.2.16 |
Because of being actionless. | KVs 7.2.17 |
And because of the usage 'In the absence [of something], [it] does not exist.' | KVs 7.2.18 |
Word and meaning are not [intrinsically] connected. | KVs 7.2.19 |

body.text: saṃyogino daṇḍāt samavāyino viṣāṇāc ca | KVs_7,2.20 |
body.translated_text: [This follows] from [the distinction between] the stick conjoined [with the substance] and the horn inherent [in the substance]. | KVs 7.2.20 |
Since it is observed, [the connection between word and meaning] is not a cause; [it is merely] a convention (<s>pratyaya</s>). | KVs 7.2.21 |
Likewise, the absence of convention. | KVs 7.2.22 |
If [one argues] from the relation of that which is related — there is doubt. | KVs 7.2.23 |
The cognition of meaning from a word is conventional (<s>sāmayika</s>). | KVs 7.2.24 |
'Farther' and 'nearer' [arise] from two things in one direction and at one time, from one that is proximate and one that is remote. | KVs 7.2.25 |
And because of the farther-ness of the cause, and the nearer-ness of the cause. | KVs 7.2.26 |
The absence of farther-ness and nearer-ness in farther-ness and nearer-ness has been explained by [analogy with] atomic-ness and great-ness. | KVs 7.2.27 |
Actions by actions, qualities by qualities. | KVs 7.2.28 |

body.text: iheti yataḥ kāryakāraṇayoḥ sa samavāyaḥ | KVs_7,2.29 |
body.translated_text: 'This [inheres] in that' — from which [relation] the cause and effect [are so related], that is <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). | KVs 7.2.29 |
The denial of substance-ness, quality-ness, and action-ness [of inherence] has been explained by its reality (<s>bhāva</s>). | KVs 7.2.30 |
And its true nature (<s>tattva</s>). | KVs 7.2.31 |
Knowledge in substances has been explained. | KVs 8.1 |
The mind (<s>manas</s>) and the self (<s>ātman</s>) [are the instruments of knowledge]. | KVs 8.2 |
In the exposition of knowledge, the method of the production of knowledge has been stated. | KVs 8.3 |

body.text: guṇakarmasv asannikṛṣṭeṣu jñānaniṣpatter dravyaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāraṇakāraṇaṃ ca | KVs_8.4 |
body.translated_text: When qualities and actions are not in contact [with the senses], substance is the cause and the cause of the cause of the production of knowledge. | KVs 8.4 |

body.text: sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu sāmānyaviśeṣābhāvāt tata eva jñānam | KVs_8.5 |
body.translated_text: In universals and particulars, because of the absence of [further] universals and particulars, that [knowledge] is just from that. | KVs 8.5 |
[Knowledge] depends on universals and particulars in substances, qualities, and actions. | KVs 8.6 |
In substance, [knowledge] depends on substance, quality, and action. | KVs 8.7 |

body.text: guṇakarmasu guṇakarmābhāvad guṇakarmāpekṣaṃ na vidyate | KVs_8.8 |
body.translated_text: In qualities and actions, because of the absence of [further] qualities and actions, dependence on qualities and actions does not exist. | KVs 8.8 |

body.text: samavāyinaḥ śvaityāc chvaityabuddheḥ śvete buddhis te kāryakāraṇabhūte | KVs_8.9 |
body.translated_text: From the whiteness of an inherent [substance], the cognition of whiteness; and in what is white, the cognition — these two stand in the relation of cause and effect. | KVs 8.9 |
In substances, [cognitions] are not mutually caused, and because of the non-simultaneity of causes. | KVs 8.10 |
Likewise in substances, qualities, and actions, because of the non-specificity of causes. | KVs 8.11 |

body.text: ayam eṣa kṛtaṃ tvayā bhojayāinam iti buddhyapekṣaṃ | KVs_8.12 |
body.translated_text: 'This is he,' 'done by you,' 'feed him' — [these] depend on cognition. | KVs 8.12 |
Because of existence in what is perceived, and absence in what is not perceived. | KVs 8.13 |
'Object' (<s>artha</s>) [is used] with reference to substances, qualities, and actions. | KVs 8.14 |
The five-element nature of substances has been denied. | KVs 8.15 |

body.text: bhūyastvād gandhavattvāc ca pṛthivī gandhajñāne | KVs_8.16 |
body.translated_text: Because of predominance and because of possessing smell, earth is [the basis] in the cognition of smell. | KVs 8.16 |

body.text: tathāpas tejo vāyuś ca rasarūpasparśajñāneṣu rasarūpasparśaviśeṣāt | KVs_8.17 |
body.translated_text: Likewise water, fire, and air, with respect to taste, color, and touch [respectively], due to the specificity of taste, color, and touch [in those substances]. | KVs 8.17 |
Prior to [its production, the effect] is non-existent, because of the absence of designation of action and quality. | KVs 9.1 |
[It is] existent and non-existent. | KVs 9.2 |
From the existent, the non-existent [is distinct], because of the absence of designation of action and quality — [it is] a distinct category. | KVs 9.3 |
[What is] existent and non-existent. | KVs 9.4 |

body.text: yac cānyat satas tad apy asat | KVs_9.5 |
body.translated_text: And that which is other than the existent, that too is non-existent. | KVs 9.5 |

body.text: asad iti bhūtapratyakṣābhāvād bhūtasmṛter virodhipratyakṣatvāc ca jñānam | KVs_9.6 |
body.translated_text: '[It is] non-existent' — because of the absence of perception of [something] that has come into being, and because it has the character of perception opposed to the memory of [something] that has been — [such is the] knowledge. | KVs 9.6 |
And because of the perception of existence in such absence. | KVs 9.7 |
By this, 'non-pot,' 'non-cow,' and '<s>adharma</s>' (demerit) are explained. | KVs 9.8 |
'What has not come into being does not exist' — this is not a separate meaning. | KVs 9.9 |

body.text: nāsti ghaṭo geha iti sato ghaṭasya gehasaṃyogapratiṣedhaḥ | KVs_9.10 |
body.translated_text: 'There is no pot in the house' — this is the negation of the conjunction of the [existing] pot with the house. | KVs 9.10 |

body.text: nāsty anyaś candramā iti sāmānyāc candramasaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ | KVs_9.11 |
body.translated_text: 'There is no other moon' — this is the negation from the universal of moon-ness. | KVs 9.11 |

body.text: sad asator vaidharmyāt kārye sad asattā na | KVs_9.12 |
body.translated_text: Because of the mutual distinction of the existent and the non-existent, the non-existence [of the effect] does not exist in the [existent] effect. | KVs 9.12 |
In the self, from a particular conjunction of the self and the mind, [arises] perception of the self. | KVs 9.13 |
Likewise, in other substances. | KVs 9.14 |
And from the contact of the self, the sense organ, the mind, and the object. | KVs 9.15 |
From inherence in that [self], [arises knowledge] of actions and qualities. | KVs 9.16 |
From inherence in the self, [arises knowledge] of the qualities of the self. | KVs 9.17 |

body.text: asyedaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃbandhy ekārhtasamavāyi virodhi ceti laiṅgikam | KVs_9.18 |
body.translated_text: 'This is the effect of that,' 'this is the cause of that,' 'this is related to that,' 'this co-inheres in one object with that,' 'this is opposed to that' — [these are] inferential (<s>laiṅgika</s>). | KVs 9.18 |
By this, verbal testimony (<s>śābda</s>) is explained. | KVs 9.19 |

body.text: hetur apadeśo liṅgaṃ nimittaṃ pramāṇaṃ kāraṇam ity anarthāntaram | KVs_9.20 |
body.translated_text: Reason (<s>hetu</s>), designation (<s>apadeśa</s>), mark (<s>liṅga</s>), indicator (<s>nimitta</s>), means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — [these are] not different [in meaning]. | KVs 9.20 |
'This belongs to that' — because it depends on cognition. | KVs 9.21 |

body.text: ātmamanasoḥ saṃyogaviśeṣāt saṃskārāc ca smṛtiḥ | KVs_9.22 |
body.translated_text: Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) [arises] from a particular conjunction of the self and the mind, and from [mental] impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). | KVs 9.22 |
Likewise, dream (<s>svapna</s>); and [dream is close to] waking (<s>svapnāntika</s>). | KVs 9.23 |
And from <s>dharma</s> (merit). // KVs 9.24 //
From defects of the sense-organs and from <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression), [there arises] <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // KVs 9.25 //
That is defective knowledge. // KVs 9.26 //
[That which is] not defective is <s>vidyā</s> (true knowledge). // KVs 9.27 //
The knowledge of <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) and the vision of <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings) [arise] from <s>dharmas</s> (merits). // KVs 9.28 //

body.text: ātmasamavāyaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pañcabhyo 'rthāntaratve hetus tadāśrayibhyaś ca guṇebhyaḥ | KVs_10.1 |
body.translated_text: The inherence in the <s>ātman</s> (self) is the reason for <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>duḥkha</s> (pain) being different from the five [sense-objects], and [also different] from the qualities residing in those [sense-objects]. // KVs 10.1 //

body.text: iṣṭāniṣṭakāraṇaviśeṣād virodhāc ca mithaḥ sukhaduḥkhayor arthāntarabhāvaḥ | KVs_10.2 |
body.translated_text: From the specific difference of desirable and undesirable causes, and from mutual opposition, [there is established] the distinct nature of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>duḥkha</s> (pain). // KVs 10.2 //

body.text: saṃśayanirṇayayor arthāntarabhāvaś ca jñānāntaratve hetuḥ | KVs_10.3 |
body.translated_text: And the distinct nature of doubt and certainty is the reason for [their being] different kinds of knowledge. // KVs 10.3 //

body.text: tayor niṣpattiḥ pratyakṣalaiṅgikābhyāṃ jñānāntaratve hetuḥ | KVs_10.4 |
body.translated_text: The production of those two [doubt and certainty] from perception and inference is the reason for [their being] different kinds of knowledge. // KVs 10.4 //
[The cognition] 'it was' — perception has [thus] been explained. // KVs 10.5 //
[The cognition] 'it will be' — because [such inference] has been observed in other effects. // KVs 10.6 //
[The cognition] 'it is [happening] thus' — from [causes] both dependent and independent. // KVs 10.7 //
[The cognition] 'it was not' — from [the mark of] non-existence. // KVs 10.8 //
And [the cognition 'it was not'] when [the cause] exists, from the non-inherence of the effect [in it]. // KVs 10.9 //

body.text: ekārthasamavāyiṣu kāraṇāntareṣu darśanād ekadeśa ity ekasmin | KVs_10.10 |
body.translated_text: From the observation that among things inhering in the same object there are other causes, [one infers] 'it is a part' with respect to one [whole]. // KVs 10.10 //

body.text: śiraḥ pṛṣṭham udaraṃ pāṇir iti tadviśeṣebhyaḥ | KVs_10.11 |
body.translated_text: 'Head,' 'back,' 'belly,' 'hand' — from the specific differences of those [parts]. // KVs 10.11 //
[The cognition] 'it is a cause' — from the inherence of the effect in the substance. // KVs 10.12 //
Or from conjunction. // KVs 10.13 //
From the inherence [of the effect] in the cause, [one infers] action. // KVs 10.14 //
Likewise with respect to color, and from the inherence in the cause of the cause. // KVs 10.15 //
From the inherence in the cause, [one infers] conjunction. // KVs 10.16 //
Likewise, and from the inherence in what is not the cause of the cause. // KVs 10.17 //
From the inherence in what is conjoined, [one infers] the specific [nature] of fire. // KVs 10.18 //
Inferential knowledge (<s>laiṅgika pramāṇa</s>) has [thus] been explained. // KVs 10.19 //

body.text: dṛṣṭānāṃ dṛṣṭaprayojanānāṃ dṛṣṭābhāve prayogo 'bhyudayāya (S omits dṛṣṭaprayojanānāṃ) | KVs_10.20 |
body.translated_text: The employment of seen [means] having seen purposes, in the absence of seen [purposes], is for [the attainment of] prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>). // KVs 10.20 //

body.text: tadvacanād āmnāyaprāmāṇyam iti (U,S āmnāyasya prāmāṇyam) | KVs_10.21 |
body.translated_text: From His word, [comes] the authoritativeness of the <s>Āmnāya</s> (Vedic tradition). // KVs 10.21 //
